Problem: Complex support cases require live-agent attention across systems.
RootCauseHypothesis: Support case state was historically distributed across disconnected tools, creating context-switching and inconsistent handling.
EvidenceSummary: DoorDash states agents historically navigated multiple disconnected internal and third-party tools and that the new platform aimed to eliminate fragmentation and create a single source of truth.
InternalValidation: For one incident ID, compare the number of systems touched, handoffs, agent context switches, resolution time and reopen rate.
RecommendedControl: Canonical case state plus shared evidence timeline across channels.
SuccessKPI: First-contact resolution; reopen rate; handoffs per case; time to resolution.

Problem: Legitimate activity can be blocked by overly conservative fraud logic.
RootCauseHypothesis: Fast-changing high-stakes rules require controlled versioning, backtesting, shadow evaluation and gradual rollout.
EvidenceSummary: DoorDash says excessively conservative rules sometimes blocked legitimate activity and that broad conditions can affect thousands of legitimate users quickly.
InternalValidation: Measure rule-level false-positive proxy, appeal overturn, impacted segments, and decision changes across rule versions.
RecommendedControl: Versioned rules, backtesting, shadow mode, experiments, audit logs and rollback.
SuccessKPI: False-positive rate; appeal overturn; precision/recall; rollback frequency.

Problem: Promotion accounting can require manual reconciliation.
RootCauseHypothesis: Promotion identity and funding allocation must stay consistent across DoorDash, integrations/POS and merchant accounting, including co-funded and stacked promos.
EvidenceSummary: DoorDash says promotion reconciliation can be time-consuming and may require additional labor; new structured funding fields were introduced for downstream reconciliation.
InternalValidation: At order level, reconcile displayed discount, promo IDs, merchant-funded amount, DoorDash-funded amount, refunds and final settlement.
RecommendedControl: Immutable order-level promotion ledger and funding reconciliation before close.
SuccessKPI: Unreconciled promo dollars; manual reconciliation hours; mismatch rate.

Problem: Merchant error charges can be disputed after responsibility assignment.
RootCauseHypothesis: When evidence is partial, automated responsibility assignment should expose confidence and allow evidence-based review.
EvidenceSummary: DoorDash documents claim evaluation using photos, error type and fraud criteria; merchant error charges may be disputed if responsibility is believed incorrect.
InternalValidation: Compare evidence completeness, decision confidence, dispute rate, dispute overturn and repeated issue patterns by item/store/Dasher.
RecommendedControl: Evidence completeness scoring, confidence routing and structured disputes.
SuccessKPI: Dispute overturn; low-confidence auto-charge rate; resolution time.

Problem: Customer fees can vary with distance, order size, merchant, membership and local regulation.
RootCauseHypothesis: Technically valid dynamic pricing can still create perceived inconsistency if reasons and savings are not transparent.
EvidenceSummary: DoorDash states exact fees depend on merchant, DashPass status and local regulations, and that updated service fees can vary with distance and order size.
InternalValidation: Compare displayed fee explanation, expected rule output, checkout authorization and settled amount; separate valid variation from rule violations.
RecommendedControl: Price-rule traceability, transparent reason codes and displayed-to-settled reconciliation.
SuccessKPI: Displayed-to-settled variance; fee-related contact rate; checkout abandonment.

Problem: DashPass does not mean zero total fees.
RootCauseHypothesis: Membership value must be explained at the eligible-order level, not inferred from the existence of a subscription.
EvidenceSummary: DoorDash says eligible orders get $0 delivery fees and reduced service fees, subject to DashPass merchant and subtotal requirements.
InternalValidation: Track eligible vs ineligible orders, expected benefit, realized savings and contacts after benefit non-application.
RecommendedControl: Eligibility pre-check and explicit savings bridge at checkout.

Problem: Marketplace commission and menu markup can create demand/margin tension.
RootCauseHypothesis: Merchant margin pressure and customer price sensitivity can work against each other even when systems operate correctly.
EvidenceSummary: DoorDash current merchant plans list 15%, 25% and 30% delivery commission tiers and 6% pickup.
InternalValidation: Model merchant contribution margin and incremental demand by plan, markup, promo spend and reorder behavior.
RecommendedControl: Merchant profitability cockpit and pricing guardrails.

Problem: DoorDash study associates menu markup with lower sales and reorder.
RootCauseHypothesis: Markup can protect merchant unit economics while reducing conversion and retention.
EvidenceSummary: DoorDash cites a 2023 internal study of 4,500+ restaurants in which marked-up restaurants could see up to 37% fewer sales and up to 78% lower reorder rates.
InternalValidation: Estimate causal effect by merchant cohort, category, geography and baseline margin rather than generalizing the maximum reported effect.
RecommendedControl: Test pricing interventions and merchant-specific margin/reorder tradeoffs.
SuccessKPI: Sales; reorder; contribution margin; price gap vs in-store.

Problem: BBB shows a large complaint-channel volume across product, service, delivery and billing categories.
RootCauseHypothesis: Complaint-channel data can identify themes but cannot establish platform-wide defect prevalence or causality.
EvidenceSummary: BBB profile currently lists 21,839 complaints over three years with category breakdown. BBB also notes displayed complaints may not represent all filed complaints.
InternalValidation: Join complaint theme coding to an internal denominator: eligible orders/users and verified incident outcomes.
RecommendedControl: Use complaint data only as hypothesis generation, then validate against internal event and case data.
SuccessKPI: Verified incidents per eligible order; complaint-to-confirmed ratio.
